achieve_passing_justification: The project has the passing badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15627
contribution_requirements_justification: Contribution requirements, including coding style and tests, are in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
dco_justification: Every commit must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked on every pull request by the DCO app: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: The maintainer-led governance model and how decisions are made: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities, and who holds them: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer holds the access to the repository, npm organisation and domain today. Releases use npm trusted publishing (no personal token) and the code is MIT-licensed, but no second person holds access yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: What the project plans to do, and not do, until October 2027, with the work tracked in GitHub issues and the 1.0 milestone (https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/milestone/1): https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: Packages, dependencies, design, build and release: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/architecture
documentation_security_justification: What users can and cannot rely on: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
documentation_current_justification: The API reference is generated from the source with TypeDoc, and CI fails on TypeDoc warnings such as broken links (npm run docs:check). Numbers in the "In practice" examples and tutorials are checked by tests. Documentation defects are fixed as normal changes.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README links the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The docs site uses VitePress semantic HTML, WCAG AA contrast themes for code, light and dark modes, and respects prefers-reduced-motion. The libraries are code with no user interface.
internationalization_justification: The libraries return numbers and typed data, not text for end users, and do not sort human-readable text. The MCP tool descriptions are for AI assistants.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub, npm and a static docs site) store no passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Each major is supported as a whole: fixes ship as a new patch or minor, and upgrading within a major never breaks. The previous major gets high and critical security fixes for 6 months after the next major, and deprecated APIs keep working for one full major. The upgrade path between majors is in the upgrading guide, the release notes and each package changelog: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/upgrading
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been reported to the project in the last 12 months; the repository has no security advisories. Fixes in that period patched published advisories in upstream development dependencies.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Reports are made privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email. Acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment, a fix in a private GitHub security advisory, coordinated disclosure and credit: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: Code follows the project ESLint configuration (eslint-config-phun-ky, including Prettier) and strict TypeScript, and must pass npm run lint and npm run typecheck: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The Checks workflow runs ESLint (with Prettier through eslint-plugin-prettier) and the TypeScript compiler in strict mode on every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires it to pass before merging.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are built; the project compiles TypeScript to JavaScript.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The TypeScript build emits source maps and declaration files alongside the JavaScript; nothing is stripped or minified.
build_non_recursive_justification: npm run build runs tsc -b with TypeScript project references, building each package once in dependency order.
build_repeatable_justification: The TypeScript compiler is deterministic and dependencies are pinned in package-lock.json (npm ci in CI); rebuilding the same source gives identical output.
installation_common_justification: Packages are installed and removed with npm, e.g. npm install @interstellar-tools/equations and npm uninstall @interstellar-tools/equations.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done entirely by npm, which honours its standard location settings (--prefix, npm_config_prefix, global vs. local). The packages have no install scripts and only publish dist.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm install, npm run build and npm test give the full development and test environment: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/development
external_dependencies_justification: Dependencies are listed in package.json and package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks npm dependencies weekly, and CodeQL and the OpenSSF Scorecard run in CI. Known advisories are fixed promptly, e.g. #115 and #137.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository; all external components come from npm through package.json and the lockfile, and Dependabot opens update pull requests.
interfaces_current_justification: The code uses current interfaces: ES modules with NodeNext resolution, Node 24, TypeScript 6, current GitHub Actions. Deprecated APIs are avoided, e.g. the MCP host check is implemented in the project instead of with the deprecated SDK transport option.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Checks workflow builds, lints, type-checks, checks the API docs and runs the tests on every push to main and every pull request, reporting results as GitHub checks with coverage uploaded to Codecov.
regression_tests_added50_justification: In the last six months, 7 of the 10 bugs fixed in the published packages got a regression test, e.g. the planet angles (#145), the time step unit (#144) and the MCP DNS rebinding fix.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Line coverage measured with Node built-in coverage: constants 100%, equations 99.98%, mcp about 90%, temporal 100%, types 100%; reports are uploaded to Codecov on every CI run.
test_policy_mandated_justification: New functionality must come with tests and bug fixes with a regression test: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_documented_added_justification: The tests policy is part of the instructions for contributing code: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript runs with strict: true and TypeDoc treats warnings as errors in CI. The package sources have no ESLint warnings; the remaining warnings are console output in build scripts and documentation examples.
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles applied (economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, least privilege, open design, limited attack surface): https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
crypto_used_network_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
crypto_tls12_justification: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The software implements and uses no cryptography. Network transport security for a public MCP server is provided by the HTTPS proxy or tunnel in front of it.
signed_releases_justification: Packages are published from GitHub Actions with npm trusted publishing and carry Sigstore-signed provenance; the signing identity comes from GitHub OIDC, not a key on npm. Verification with npm audit signatures is documented: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not signed; releases are verified through npm provenance instead.
input_validation_justification: Equations check their inputs and throw on non-finite or out-of-domain values. The MCP server validates every tool input against a Zod schema with ranges and enumerations, and over HTTP rejects requests whose Host header is not allowed.
hardening_justification: Strict TypeScript, no eval or dynamic code, no runtime dependencies outside the monorepo for the libraries, read-only datasets, and an MCP server that only calculates, binds to 127.0.0.1 and checks the Host header. CodeQL scans every change.
assurance_case_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles and the common weaknesses countered: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses the JavaScript/TypeScript code and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/security/code-scanning
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: All software is TypeScript on JavaScript runtimes, which are memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The maintainer, the only person with access, uses two-factor authentication on GitHub, which GitHub requires for code contributors. Anyone given access later must use it too: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires a role to be chosen for every collaborator invited to the repository, and the governance requires the lowest role that fits: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires changes to arrive through a pull request with passing checks. Only the maintainer, as administrator, and the release workflow can bypass it.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The ruleset on main blocks deleting the branch and force pushes.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow interpolates untrusted metadata, such as pull request titles or branch names, into a script; github.actor is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests run on the pull_request event, where forks get no secrets. The labeler runs on pull_request_target but never checks out or runs pull request code, with only pull-requests: write. Publishing runs only after a merge: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/label.yml
osps_br_03_01_justification: All official channels use HTTPS: the GitHub repository, the npm packages and the documentation site at https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/
osps_br_03_02_justification: Packages are distributed by npm over HTTPS, and each carries a Sigstore-signed provenance attestation: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled and blocks commits that contain secrets; secrets are kept only in GitHub Actions secrets: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_01_01_justification: User guides for every package, the MCP server and the API reference: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/
osps_do_02_01_justification: How to report a bug, with an issue template: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage problems are discussed in public GitHub issues and pull requests: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/issues
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT licence, which is OSI-approved: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released npm packages are under the MIT licence, declared in each package.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: The licence is in the LICENSE file at the repository root: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: Every package includes the licence text in its LICENSE file, published with it to npm: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/packages/equations/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_02_justification: The full git history, with authors and dates, is public: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Direct dependencies are listed in each package.json, with every version locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/package.json
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project has a single repository, a monorepo holding all five packages.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executables are committed: build output (dist) is ignored, and packages are built in CI.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are PNG images for the documentation site; there are no executables, archives or other unreviewable binaries.
osps_vm_02_01_justification: Security contacts (email and GitHub private vulnerability reporting): https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The repository defaults GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only, and every workflow sets read-only permissions at the top level, with jobs asking only for what they need: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every release has a unique Semantic Versioning version per package, tagged as @interstellar-tools/<package>@<version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/releases
osps_br_04_01_justification: Each package has a CHANGELOG.md, generated from conventional commits, listing features, fixes and breaking changes, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/packages/equations/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are installed with npm ci from the lockfile in every pipeline: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every package is published with a Sigstore-signed provenance attestation, verifiable with npm audit signatures: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_06_01_justification: How dependencies are chosen, obtained and tracked: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_do_07_01_justification: Build instructions with the required Node.js, npm and Git versions: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/development
osps_gv_01_01_justification: Who has access to the repository, the npm organisation and the domain: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
osps_gv_01_02_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_03_02_justification: Requirements for code contributions: style, tests, sign-off, commits and pull requests: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires the status checks (Checks, Dependency Review and DCO) and CodeQL results to pass before merging; only an administrator can bypass it.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: The Checks workflow builds and runs every test suite on every pull request, and must pass before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
osps_sa_01_01_justification: The architecture (packages, actors, build and release) and the trust boundaries between contributors, CI, npm, users and MCP clients: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/architecture
osps_sa_02_01_justification: Every exported function and type is described in the API reference, and the MCP server's tools, resources and HTTP interface in its guide: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/mcp/
osps_sa_03_01_justification: The assurance case assesses the most likely and impactful security problems: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: Coordinated disclosure, with acknowledgement within 7 days and a fix within 30 days for serious issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the security email: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories when fixed: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/security/advisories
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Each job declares only the permissions it needs, e.g. the labeler has pull-requests: write and publishing has id-token: write: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/label.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Workflows take no manual inputs, and the only collaborator-controlled value used, github.actor, is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: Each release is a versioned npm package and a GitHub release with the same tag, and its SBOM is named <package>-<version>.cdx.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/releases
osps_br_07_02_justification: How secrets are stored, accessed, scoped and rotated: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_03_01_justification: How to verify release integrity with npm audit signatures: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_03_02_justification: How to check that a release was built by the publish workflow in phun-ky/interstellar-tools, from its provenance: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_04_01_justification: Each release is supported until the next release of the same package: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: A release stops getting security updates when the next release of the same package is published: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_gv_04_01_justification: Collaborators are reviewed, including two-factor authentication, before getting escalated permissions: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every GitHub release has a CycloneDX SBOM of the package's runtime dependencies attached, generated by the publish workflow: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has a single repository, so there are no subprojects in other repositories.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: When and how the tests run, locally and in CI: https://phun-ky.net/interstellar-tools/guide/development#test-the-code
osps_qa_06_03_justification: New functionality and bug fixes must come with tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The project has one maintainer, so no non-author approval is possible yet. The ruleset will require one approval once there is a second maintainer: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_sa_03_02_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries and attack surface: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#threat-model
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Vulnerabilities in dependencies that don't affect the project are recorded as OpenVEX statements in vex.openvex.json; there are none at the moment: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_01_justification: Thresholds for fixing vulnerability and licence findings in dependencies: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Releases are blocked while a runtime dependency has a known high or critical vulnerability (npm audit in the publish workflow): https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Dependency review checks every pull request against the GitHub Advisory Database and blocks high or critical findings, as the documented policy says: https://github.com/phun-ky/interstellar-tools/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
